text: What does cannabis do to my brain?

args.label: Cannabis (THC), example

targets.effect: Binds CB1 receptors: high, short memory, slower coordination, hunger
Raises heart rate for an hour or two

args.source: Huestis 2007, Chem Biodivers: smoked THC bioavailability 10-35%, peak plasma within ~3-10 min, Vd ~3.4 L/kg; 2 h is an effective half-life for the fast fall after peak, the terminal half-life is much longer

args.label: Cannabis high (example)
args.source: Own estimate guided by Huestis 2007: heart rate up about 20 bpm peaking 10-30 min after smoking, effects over 2-4 h, hunger and drowsiness after

feelings.label: High
feelings.cause: THC switching on cannabinoid receptors in the brain

feelings.label: Hungry
feelings.cause: THC boosts appetite signals and food reward

stops.label: Lungs
stops.say: THC crosses from the air sacs into the blood within seconds.

stops.label: Heart
stops.say: Blood carries it from the lungs to the heart, which speeds up.

stops.label: Brain
stops.say: It reaches the brain and sits on cannabinoid receptors, damping signalling.

steps.title: An example puff, now
steps.say: I added an example inhaled dose at 21:10. THC passes from the air sacs into the blood within seconds, which is why smoking feels fast.

composed.caption: THC crossing from air sac into blood
composed.basis: Huestis 2007: smoked THC peaks in plasma within minutes; smoke irritation of airway lining is textbook pulmonology

steps.title: The heart speeds up
steps.say: Blood from the lungs goes straight to the heart, then the brain. THC widens vessels and nudges the heart from about 78 to about 98 beats.

steps.title: THC borrows a brake
steps.say: Your brain has its own cannabinoids, which act as a brake on nerve signals. THC fits the same CB1 receptors and presses that brake everywhere at once.

composed.caption: THC on the nerve ending's CB1 brake
composed.basis: Textbook endocannabinoid signalling: CB1 receptors on nerve endings reduce messenger release (Wilson and Nicoll 2002)

steps.title: Where the brake lands
steps.say: CB1 is dense in memory, timing and movement areas, so short-term memory slips and coordination slows. Less braking on reward cells releases extra dopamine: the high.

composed.caption: Brake lifted on reward cells, dopamine rises
composed.basis: Disinhibition of ventral tegmental dopamine cells by CB1 on GABA terminals (Lupica and Riegel 2005); amounts are illustration

steps.title: Later: hungry, then sleepy
steps.say: Within the hour CB1 in the hunger centre may make food taste better and you may feel hungry. As it fades, you may feel drowsy; your beer adds to that.

lines.text: THC sticks to your brain's own braking receptors and dampens signals in memory, coordination and reward areas.
After this example puff, your heart may go from about 78 to 98 beats.
You may feel high, then hungry, then sleepy. Tonight's beer would add to the wobbliness.
